parsed.rationale: The method already lazily decodes parameters only once and returns the cached map; no unnecessary allocations or work can be removed without altering semantics.
Inlines the counterOffset(i) computation, using a running offset instead of a method call and per‑iteration shift, reducing loop overhead.
Replaced Arrays.copyOf with the faster array.clone() to eliminate extra method overhead and length checks, and hoisted the length of oldChildren to a local variable to reduce repeated field accesses.
Rewrites the double‑while logic into a single streamlined loop, removing redundant variables and branches, which reduces per‑iteration overhead.
Reordered checks to avoid the potentially expensive expiration test when the node's value is null, eliminating an unnecessary method call in that case.

Removed the redundant catch‑block for DecoderException and merged its handling into the generic Exception catch, reducing bytecode and a needless stack‑trace allocation. The logic remains identical while eliminating an unnecessary try‑catch path.
Adds fast‑path checks for ranges that start at 0 or end at the maximum, avoiding one call to Util.cardinalityInBitmapRange and thus saving work on common edge cases.
Unrolled the main loop to reduce per-iteration overhead and branch mispredictions, handling remaining bytes in a tail loop.
Added fast‑path checks for empty containers to avoid unnecessary array allocation and merging, and used direct field access instead of virtual getCardinality calls.
The method already performs the minimal work needed to execute either a Callable or a Runnable without extra allocations or checks.

Rewritten to use early returns, eliminating the need for a separate index variable after the loop and reducing branching. This streamlines the control flow and marginally improves hot‑path performance.
The original implementation is already optimal for its responsibilities; no unnecessary allocations or work are performed.
Caches the value produced by factory and function so it is computed only once per retry loop, avoiding repeated expensive calls on CAS failures.
Inlines the putIfMatch call to avoid an extra method call and duplicate null‑check, directly invoking the low‑level putIfMatch0 logic. This reduces call overhead on the hot putIfAbsent path.

Adds a fast‑path for heap byte[] buffers that writes directly to the array, eliminating the per‑byte PlatformDependent.putByte call and its bounds checks, while keeping the off‑heap unsafe path unchanged.
Iterates directly over the underlying list using index arithmetic, eliminating the call to ListIterate.forEach and any iterator allocation.
Caches the result of the initial cast for each branch, avoiding repeated casts and streamlining the instanceof checks for slightly lower overhead.
Clears the queue by bulk‑nulling the range of slots and atomically advancing the consumer index, avoiding the per‑element poll overhead and CAS on each iteration.

Defers creating and clearing the temporary bitmap until a key has at least two contributing containers. Keys present in only one input use that container's cardinality directly, avoiding temporary-container allocation, bitmap clearing, OR work, and lazy repair without mutating the input.

The method already performs only the necessary successor lookup and eviction. Capturing the successor before eviction preserves traversal when eviction unlinks the node; no safe optimization is evident.

Adds an empty-bucket fast path that skips both transfers and their cleanup when neither list contains nodes. This reduces work when advancing over sparse timer wheels while preserving the limit check and existing nonempty-list handling.

Moves the invariant expected-value test outside the loop, allowing each loop to branch directly on the predicate result. Preserves traversal order, short-circuiting, and predicate invocation counts; the benefit depends on whether the JIT already performs this specialization.

This method allocates nothing, and the JVM can inline both the sentinel conversion and Objects.equals. Without the sentinel conversion implementation, there is no clear optimization that preserves all equality semantics.

Returns immediately on a matching chain entry, avoiding the post-loop length check on hits. Loads each candidate once and consolidates insertion bookkeeping while preserving callback and table-update ordering.

Uses the loop's readable-byte count as the pre-decode length, avoiding a separate isReadable() call when no output needs forwarding. Refreshes the length after forwarding output because downstream handlers may modify the buffer, and retains the handler-removal and decode-progress checks.

Tests live indices first, reducing the common occupied-slot path from two sentinel comparisons to one. Caches the arrays and capacity mask across collision probes while preserving the probe sequence, stored-key equality direction, and tombstone selection.

Appends contiguous runs of unreserved characters in bulk instead of calling StringBuilder.append for every character, enabling bulk copying for String inputs. Single-character runs retain the direct append path, and UTF-8 encoding and malformed-surrogate handling remain unchanged.

Reads the current state before attempting CAS, avoiding both failed atomic operations for already-completed promises and the initial failed CAS for uncancellable promises. Retains the fallback CAS to handle a concurrent transition from null to UNCANCELLABLE.
Inlines the linking operation and caches the bucket's tail, eliminating a repeated virtual getter after intervening pointer writes. Preserves the original pointer-update order.

Adds a fast path for updating the bucket's first entry, reusing the bucket read and directly sharing its unchanged tail. This avoids the slow-path bucket reread and replacement-chain helper on common existing-key updates while retaining the original retry and resize handling.
The method already performs one required allocation and a bulk buffer copy. Retaining it also preserves the buffer position, mark, and underflow behavior without adding fast-path checks.

The method already performs one lookup per key, updates the result in place, reads the ticker once, and batches statistics and drain scheduling. No clear further optimization is justified by the supplied context without risking expiration, refresh, or concurrency semantics.

Computes the key-table offset once instead of rereading the serialization cookie for each non-run container. Direct cardinality reads also eliminate redundant container-index validation, since callers already validate k and the loop visits only preceding containers.

An empty look-ahead slot proves that slot itself, as well as the preceding slots, is available to the single producer. Caching the exclusive limit one position beyond it avoids one redundant volatile probe per look-ahead batch, while reusing the current element offset on the fallback path.

Hoists buffer acquisition out of the magazine-probing loop, removing the repeated null check on failed allocation attempts. The buffer is still obtained from the first magazine probed, and retry, expansion, and release behavior remain unchanged.
This method directly delegates to the backing cache without allocations or redundant work. The JVM can inline the delegation; no useful optimization is available within this method alone.

Hoists the cardinality, content array and bitmap field into locals so they are not reloaded each iteration, and replaces the division by 64 with a shift. This removes redundant field loads and lets the JIT eliminate more bounds checks.

The method already reuses a per-handler output list, so it allocates nothing on the normal path and does only a few cheap checks. Any further change would be negligible or risk altering the exception semantics, so it is returned unchanged.

After a rehash, uses probeForRehash instead of probe, avoiding key equals() calls along the collision chain since the key is known absent and no tombstones exist. Also inlines the capacity check and caches fields in locals to cut repeated field loads and helper calls.
Hoists the table field into a local array and loads each element once instead of twice. This lets the JIT drop bounds checks and avoids re-reading the field and element every iteration.

Builds the class-name key from a small char[] (which escape analysis can scalar-replace) instead of a StringBuilder with its growing internal buffer and extra copy. This cuts allocation and copying on every cache construction while producing an identical key.
The method is a thin dispatcher with cheap special cases. The real work is in helper methods that I cannot change from here, so I left it unchanged.

Every caller builds the clone with new BranchNode(this.prefixLength()), so its prefix array already has the right size. The prefix is now copied into it with System.arraycopy instead of allocating a second array, and it falls back to Arrays.copyOf if the sizes differ. The child loop also reads each array element once.
The method is a single delegation with one small adapter allocation; there is no cheaper equivalent that keeps the same semantics, so it is returned unchanged.

The method is already lock-free, creates the value at most once, and does a single chain scan per CAS attempt. Any rewrite would give only negligible gains or risk changing semantics, so it is returned unchanged.
Inlines the loop over the backing array, avoiding a static helper call, which makes the call site's predicate dispatch more specialized per list type and keeps fields in locals.
The method is already a carefully ordered dispatch with fast paths, deliberately structured around JIT instanceof behavior; no safe change would give a measurable benefit.

In the FIELD state, the charset and name attribute lookups (map lookups) were done on every call even when the attribute already existed and they were unused. They now run only when the attribute is created, so repeated calls while streaming chunks skip them.
Replaces the recursion over the chain of older tables with an iterative loop, removing call overhead and stack use. The result is the same because long addition is commutative, even with overflow.

The method allocates one small wrapper per batch, and the per-element work is just the predicate and procedure calls. An anonymous class or lambda would allocate the same object and make the same calls, so there is no measurable gain.

Adds an identity fast path before equals, reuses the already-read key instead of calling getKey() again, and hoists the repeated cast of the chain head. These are small savings in the hot lookup/update loop.
The method is a single function call and a single delegation to the map. All the cost lies in the map's updateValueWith, so there is nothing to remove here.

Reads the cumulation field once into a local in the setup and in the finally block instead of re-reading it for the null, isReadable and release checks. Behavior is preserved because the field is still re-read after decode, which may reset it. The gain is small.

Replaces the per-insert ByteBuffer allocation (buffer object plus backing array) with a plain byte[16] and shift-based packing/unpacking, and removes the temporary secondBytes array in the Node48 growth path by extracting bytes directly from the long.
